• The scientific name is **Puccinia Graminis**.
 
• It is capable of producing infectious **urediniospores** as long as infected leaf tissue remains alive.
 
• Urediniospores can be **wind-disseminated **infect host plants hundreds of kilometers from their source plants.
 
 
 
• **Fungus**:-
 
 
• There are about** 144,00 known species of organisms of the kingdom fungi** including **yeasts, rusts, smuts, mildew, molds, and mushrooms**.
 
• Fungi are among the most widely distributed organisms on earth and are of **great environmental and medical importance**.
 
• Fungi are **eukaryotic organisms** which means their **cells contain membrane-bound organelles and clearly defined nuclei**.
 
• Together with bacteria, fungi are **responsible for breaking down organic matter and releasing carbon, oxygen, nitrogen and phosphorus into the soil and the atmosphere**.

• Plant is any **multicellular eukaryotic life-form characterized by photosynthetic nutrition**.
 
• It plays a vital role in the **maintenance of life on earth**.
 
• All energy used by living organisms depends on the complex process of** photosynthesis which is mostly carried out by green plants**.
 
 
 
• **Algae**:-
 
 
• Algae are **chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic, and largely aquatic(both freshwater and marine ) organisms**.
 
• They occur in a variety of other habitats: moist stones, soils, and wood.
 
 
 
• **Animal**:-
 
 
• It is a **group of multicellular eukaryotic organisms**.
 
• They are thought to have **evolved independently from the unicellular eukaryotes**.
 
• Animals **dominate human conceptions of life on Earth** not simply by their size, abundance, and sheer diversity but also by their mobility, a trait that humans share.

questions.question: Which of the following religious communities in India primarily celebrates the Pateti festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Parsi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pateti is the **new year festival** of the Parsis.
 
• Pateti comes from the Persian word '**Patet'** which means '**confession' or 'repentance'.**
 
• On this festival, Parsis mark the beginning of the new year, go to the agyari and spend the day with family members.
 
• The Parsis don’t just believe in celebrating the new year and forgetting about the past. Rather they cherish the past and look back on the year that has passed and ask for repentance.
 
• This generally occurs just before the New year or the last day of the previous year and usually encompasses **5 days **of repentance which has now been reduced to **one**. 
 
• New year's day which historically falls on the **spring equinox** is now celebrated in **mid-August every year**.
 
• The **Shahenshahi** calendar used by the Parsis is itself known as **Nowroz.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Parsi community**

 
 
• **​**One of the most well-known minority communities in the country is the Parsis who follow the **4000-year-old** ancient **Zoroastrianism religion** from **Persia**.
 
• Zoroastrianism spread to the world via the Silk Route and influenced other religions such as Judaism and Christianity. It is a monotheistic religion established by the Prophet Zarathustra who was the contemporary of Cyrus the Great, back in 1200 BC.
 
• The Parsis, came to India after the Arab conquest started. Historians believe that they sailed across the Arabian Sea to reach **Gujarat sometime in 785 AD.** Today, around **60,000** Parsis reside in the country.
 
• The Parsis are a distinctive community in the country who are known for their distinct cuisine and way of life. Many of them such as **Jamshedji Tata** have contributed to building this nation.
 
• This community is predominantly based in the western region, especially in **Maharashtra and Gujarat.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Islam (Muslim) religion -**

 
 
• **Hazrat Muhammad Sahib **was the founder of the Islam religion.
 
• Hazrat Muhammad Sahib was born in Mecca in 570 AD.
 
• Hazrat Muhammad Sahib died in 632 AD. After his death, Islam got divided into two sects called **Sunni and Shia**.
 
• The successors of Prophet Muhammad were called **Khalifa**.
 
 
 
• **Sikh religion -**
 
 
• The credit for the establishment of the Sikh religion goes to **Guru Nanak (the first Guru).** The followers of Guru Nanak are called **Sikhs**.
 
• There are 10 Gurus in Sikhism. 10th Guru was **Guru Govind Singh Ji.**
 
• In **1699** AD, on the day of Baisakhi, Guru Gobind Singh established the **Khalsa Panth.**

• After reaching the point of saturation, rainfall happens on the sea-facing side of the mountain.
 
• The sea-facing side receives high precipitation called the **Windward Side** and the other side of the mountains receives lesser precipitation called the** Leeward Side**.

questions.question: Ecology was first described as a separate field of knowledge in _______ by the German zoologist, Ernst Haeckel.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1866__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ecology** was first described as a separate field of knowledge in **1866** by the **German zoologist, Ernst Haeckel **in his book **' Generelle Morphologie der Organismen'.**
 
• Ecology emerges from two Greek words, 'Oikos' means house, and 'logos' means study.
 
• It is the scientific study of **interactions between individuals, populations, and communities with their environment.**
 
• However, it was first introduced by Hans Reiter in 1885.

 
 

 **Subdivision of Ecology**
 **Salient Features**
 
 

 Autecology
 
 
 
• **Study of particular species or individuals in relation to their surroundings.**
 
• Species-specific and population-specific autecology are the two main methods for autecological research.
 
 
 
 

 Synecology
 
 
 
• **Study of the community of living organisms as an individual unit.**
 
• Focused on the study of biotic communities composed of interdependent plants and animals in a given region.
 
 
 
 

 Habitat Ecology
 
 
 
• Study of organisms' habitat or environment and its influence on them.
 
• Habitats can be **terrestrial, freshwater, marine, and estuarine.**

questions.question: Which Ministry implemented the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)?

__
 
• Aajeevika - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) was launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development** (MoRD), **Government of India** i**n June 2011.**
 
• NRLM aims to alleviate rural poverty and create sustainable livelihood opportunities for the rural poor.
 
• NRLM set out with an agenda to cover **7 Crore** rural poor households, across **600 districts, 6000 blocks, 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats and 6 lakh villages** in the country through self-managed **Self Help Groups (SHGs) **and federated institutions and support them for livelihoods collectives in a period of **8-10 years**.
 
• The scheme is an improved version of the earlier **Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY).**
 
• The program is supported partially by the **World Bank**.
 
• In November **2015**, the program was renamed **Deendayal Antayodaya Yojana (DAY-NRLM).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Sub-schemes under NRLM-

 
• **Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana (AGEY)**

 
 
• This scheme was initiated in 2017.
 
• It aims at providing alternative sources of livelihood to members of SHGs under the parent scheme by enabling them to offer public transport services in backward rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP)**
 
 
• The main objective of this sub-scheme is to empower women in agriculture by making systematic investments to enhance their participation and productivity.
 
• The program also seeks to create and sustain agriculture-based livelihoods concerning women in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP)**
 
 
• The objective of this sub-scheme is to promote startups in rural areas.
 
• SVEP envisions the generation of sustainable self-employment opportunities for rural poor youth, facilitating them to engage effectively with the market and help generate wealth locally.
 
 
 
• **National Rural Livelihoods Project (NRLP)**
 
 
• The NRLP is designed to create ‘proof of concept’ and build capacities at the central and state levels, to have a facilitating environment for all states and UTs to transit to the NRLM.

• **Oxidation **
 
• **Lipid biosynthesis**
 
 
 
• They **contain oxidases that help in peroxide production, and catalase that neutralizes the harmful products of oxidation reaction.**
 
• In** liver cells, peroxisomes also help in alcohol detoxification.**
 
• In **plant cells, peroxisomes have two major roles to play, i.e., conversion of fatty acids into carbohydrates in seeds and photorespiration in leaves.**

questions.question: What type of plate boundaries occur along spreading centres where plates are breaking apart and pushing upward from the mantle by magma to form a new crust?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Divergent boundaries.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Divergent boundaries** occur along spreading centers where plates are breaking apart and pushing upward from the mantle by magma to form a new crust.
 
• These boundaries are also known as **constructive boundaries.**
 
• It is formed by **tectonic plates pulling apart from each other.**
 
• It pushes apart two or more plates by the rise of magma from the Earth's mantle towards the surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transform boundaries**

 
 
• A transform boundary is formed as tectonic** plates slide horizontally past each other but parts of these plates get stuck at the places where they touch.**
 
• These boundaries are** conservative **because plate interaction occurs **without creating or destroying crust.**
 
• They don't play any role in the birth of mountains or oceans, but sometimes they can trigger large earthquakes.
 
 
 
• **Convergent boundaries**
 
 
• A convergent plate boundary is formed **when tectonic plates crash into each other.**
 
• They are also known as **destructive boundaries.**
 
• These can **create deep trenches **and the** Himalayan Mountain Range** is the best active example of the crash of continental convergent plate boundaries.
 
• These boundaries are often **subduction zones.**

• **Cell Membrane**:-

 
 
• This is the **outermost covering of the cell** that separates the contents of the cell from it's external environment.

• It also prevents the movement of some other materials.
 
• It is also called a **selectively permeable membrane**.

• The nucleus plays a **central role in cellular reproduction**, the process by which a single cell divides and forms two new cells.
 
• It has a **double-layered covering membrane **called a nuclear membrane.
 
• The nuclear membrane has pores that allow the transfer of material from inside the nucleus to its outside.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria**:-
 
 
• It is known as **the powerhouse of the cell**.
 
• They have **two membrane coverings**.
 
• The outer membrane is porous while the inner membrane is deeply folded.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes**:-
 
 
• Ribosomes are responsible for protein synthesis. They translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into proteins.
 
• Ribosomes are not membrane-bound organelles. They are made up of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
 
• They can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum (forming rough ER).

questions.question: Which of the following dances evolved from ‘Ekaharya Lasyanga’?

__
 
• According to sculptural and historical evidence available, the Bharatnatyam dance evolved from** ‘Ekaharya Lasyanga’.**
 
• This is the **classical dance form of Tamil Nadu**.
 
• This dance form is nearly 2000 years old and is viewed as the** mother of many Indian classical dance forms**.
 
• Bharatnatyam dance is referred to as** Ekaharya**, where one performer pulls on several roles in a single performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ekaharya Lasyanga is one of the forms and styles in the **Natyasastra**.
 
• In this form, there is **one actor playing many roles**.
 
• Instead of many actors presenting a dramatic story, the solo actor presents, through abhinaya, the particular dominant state - **Sthayi Bhava**.

**Kuchipudi**

 
• Kuchipudi is the **classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is a dance cum drama performance that emerged from the** Krishna district** of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• This dance form is a mixture of **Tandava **(masculine) and **Lasya** (graceful feminine).
 
• The dancers in Kuchipudi dance **occasionally speak dialogues**, but the dancers in Bharatanatyam don't.

**Kathakali**

 
• Kathakali is the **classical dance form of Kerala**.
 
• It communicates the story through **footwork and gestures of face and hands**.
 
• The features of this dance form can be traced back to Natya Shastra.
 
• The art form consists of** angika, acharya, vichika, **and** satvika, **the four aspects of abhinaya along with the Nritya and Natya aspects.

**Odissi**

 
• Odissi is the** classical dance form of Odisha.**
 
• **Gotipua** is the** precursor** to the Odissi dance.
 
• Examples of this dance can be seen in the **Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves **in Odisha.
 
• Odissi dance form represents **water**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the green algae?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The correct option is **Chlorophyceae__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The members of Chlorophyceae are commonly called green algae.
 
• They may be **u****nicellular, colonial, or filamentous**.
 
• They are usually grass-green due to the dominance of pigments **Chlorophyll a **and **b**.
 
• They have storage bodies called **Pyrenoids** located in the chloroplast.
 
• Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of the **inner layer of cellulose **and the outer layer of pectose.
 
• Usually, they reproduce by the method of **Fragmentation**.**​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

**Phaeophyceae**

 
• Phaeophyceae are **Brown Algae** found primarily in **marine habitats**.
 
• They range from simple **branched **and **filamentous.**
 
• They possess **Chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids**, and, xanthophylls.
 
• They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending on the number of xanthophylls.
 
• The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a **gelatinous coating of algin.**
 
• They reproduce **sexually**, it may be isogamous, or anisogamous.

**Rhodophyceae**

 
• Rhodophyceae are commonly called **Red Algae** because of the predominance of the red pigment.
 
• The majority of the red algae are **marine** with greater concentrations found in warmer areas.
 
• They are **multicellular **and **complex** in body structure.
 
• The food is stored as **Floridian**** Starch, **similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.
 
• The red algae usually reproduce **vegetatively** by **fragmentation**.

**Liverworts**

 
• Liverworts are **Bryophytes **commonly found in **moist shaded** areas in the hills.
 
• They are also called the **amphibians** of the plant kingdom because they can live in soil but are dependent on water for **Sexual Reproduction**.
 
• The plant body of bryophytes is like **Thallus or Erect**.
 
• They lack **true roots**, stems, or leaves but may process root-like, leaf-like, or stem-like structures.
